about: Assembly tree golden vectors. The rules: DIDSA-CAD docs/assembly-tree/spec.md. Generated by DIDSA-CAD tools/assembly_tree_vectors/generate.py from its reference implementation; never edit by hand. `trees` are GET /parts/{id}/assembly-tree responses (ids are made up); `cases` pin the spec's rules over them, one `kind` each.

cases.name: rover_collapsed
cases.why: The default: the root open, everything below collapsed; group rows, folders, bubbles on collapsed rows.

cases.name: rover_both_wheels_open
cases.why: One sub-assembly placed twice: the same child ids get distinct keys under each placement (wheel_l/hub, wheel_r/hub); an open row's bubble is its own mates only.

cases.name: rover_wheel_group_open
cases.why: A group open under one placement only: its key includes the parent's path; members are numbered Bolt M4 <1>..<4>.

cases.name: rover_four_deep_with_features
cases.why: Four levels open down to a part, with its features listed under it (keys <path>#feature:<id>); the missing cable has a generated file name: Component 2.

cases.name: rover_open_part_without_features_yet
cases.why: An open part whose features the client has not fetched: no rows under it yet, still open.

cases.name: rover_screws_group_open
cases.why: The root-level group open: key #group:s1; the renamed screw stays a row of its own where it was.

cases.name: rover_grouping_off
cases.why: Grouping switched off: the repeats are listed one by one with their numbers.

cases.name: rover_folders_open
cases.why: The root's Mates and Patterns folders open (their contents are the client's: not rows here); an open key on a row that cannot open (a missing file) is ignored.

cases.name: rover_unsaved
cases.why: Unsaved is client state: an unsaved Part's rows say unsaved over a lesser state; a worse problem below still wins the bubble.

cases.name: unsaved_bubble
cases.why: A collapsed row counts the unsaved rows below it (one per placement); a suppressed placement adds nothing above but keeps its own bubble.

cases.name: unsaved_open
cases.why: ...open: the rows themselves say unsaved; an unsaved sub-assembly Part marks its own row too.

cases.name: rover_unsaved_root
cases.why: The root's own Part unsaved: the root row says so.

cases.name: rover_no_status
cases.why: Without ?status=true: no constraint states, only missing / cycle / unsaved / fixed flags; bubbles count missing files and cycles only.

cases.name: rover_no_status_grouping_off
cases.why: Without status, grouping off.

cases.name: names
cases.why: Every name fallback: override, Part name, file name, Component N; generated names skipped; numbering per Part (or per file when missing).

cases.name: names_grouping_off
cases.why: Names do not depend on grouping when nothing reaches four.

cases.name: names_one_part_through_different_files
cases.why: A Part with a generated name placed through different files: the first placement's file name names every placement of it (a generated file name included); a renamed placement keeps its own name.

cases.name: names_one_part_through_different_files_grouped
cases.why: ...and the group takes the same name.

cases.name: states
cases.why: One row per state slot, and the precedence between them.

cases.name: states_no_status
cases.why: The same rows without status: the fixed flag is the only constraint information left.

cases.name: repeats
cases.why: Missing files group by file; a group sits where its first member was and shows its worst unsuppressed member's state; suppressed members add nothing to its bubble.

cases.name: repeats_open
cases.why: The groups open, and one sub-assembly member open inside its group.

cases.name: repeats_grouping_off
cases.why: Grouping off: four and more are listed one by one.

cases.name: cycle
cases.why: A Part placed inside itself is a cycle row: no children, red, counted on the rows above.

cases.name: cycle_collapsed
cases.why: The cycle counted on the collapsed row above it.

cases.name: deep_capped
cases.why: Stopped at the depth cap: the last node is truncated (no children listed, not expandable when it has no features).

cases.name: wide_capped
cases.why: Stopped at the node cap: only the first nodes are listed.

cases.name: suppressed
cases.why: A suppressed sub-assembly is listed (dimmed) and keeps its own bubble, but adds nothing to the rows above.

cases.name: suppressed_open
cases.why: ...open, its rows show their own states.

cases.name: single_part
cases.why: A Part opened on its own: the root row and its features.

cases.name: reveal_four_deep
cases.why: Reveal a row four levels down: open each ancestor.

cases.name: reveal_top_level
cases.why: A top-level row needs nothing opened.

cases.name: reveal_in_group
cases.why: A row inside a group: open its ancestors and the group.

cases.name: reveal_in_group_off
cases.why: ...with grouping off, only the ancestors.

cases.name: reveal_root_group
cases.why: A top-level member of a group: just the group.

cases.name: reveal_inside_group_member
cases.why: Below a member of a group: the group and the member.

cases.name: filter_empty_query
cases.why: An empty query is no filter: section 7's rows for the open keys, every match false.

cases.name: filter_spaces_only
cases.why: Only spaces is also no filter.

cases.name: filter_deep_collapsed
cases.why: A name term deep in a collapsed branch: every ancestor is listed and open, the rest of each level is not; the open keys play no part.

cases.name: filter_ignores_open_keys
cases.why: The same query with other rows open gives the same rows.

cases.name: filter_case_insensitive
cases.why: Case does not matter.

cases.name: filter_in_group
cases.why: A match inside a group lists the group row (open) and only the matching members, under the open wheel.

cases.name: filter_two_terms
cases.why: Two name terms must both be in the label (AND); the order of the words does not matter.

cases.name: filter_instance_number
cases.why: `<2>` finds the second instance of every repeated Part, inside groups and out.

cases.name: filter_term_no_match
cases.why: Nothing matches: the root alone.

cases.name: filter_grouping_off
cases.why: Grouping off: no group rows; the members are listed by their ancestors.

cases.name: filter_group_and_own_label
cases.why: A group's own label never matches (`x4`), and neither does the root's (`rover`).

cases.name: filter_missing
cases.why: `:missing`: the missing battery, and the missing cable below mast / arm / head.

cases.name: filter_errors
cases.why: `:errors`: missing, cycle, broken, over-constrained rows (the bubble's error set). A fixed, near or unsaved row is not one.

cases.name: filter_errors_no_status
cases.why: `:errors` without status finds only what section 5 lists for that case: the missing files.

cases.name: filter_warnings
cases.why: `:warnings`: state near.

cases.name: filter_unsaved
cases.why: `:unsaved`: state unsaved (the client's set).

cases.name: filter_fixed
cases.why: `:fixed`: the fixed flag, whatever the state (the mast's base is fixed and constrained both ways).

cases.name: filter_fixed_flag_without_status
cases.why: `:fixed` without status still works: it is the flag.

cases.name: filter_hidden
cases.why: `:hidden`: rows with the eye-off.

cases.name: filter_suppressed
cases.why: `:suppressed`: a suppressed sub-assembly; its children are not suppressed themselves, so they do not match.

cases.name: filter_parts
cases.why: `:parts`: kind part (not assemblies, not missing).

cases.name: filter_assemblies
cases.why: `:assemblies`: kind assembly.

cases.name: filter_token_and_name
cases.why: A token and a name term: both must hold.

cases.name: filter_two_tokens
cases.why: Two tokens: both must hold (AND).

cases.name: filter_token_case
cases.why: Tokens are case-insensitive too.

cases.name: filter_unknown_token
cases.why: An unknown token is left out of the matching and listed, lower case, once, in query order.

cases.name: filter_only_unknown_token
cases.why: Only an unknown token: a filter with no criteria matches nothing, and says what it did not understand.

cases.name: filter_lone_colon
cases.why: A lone `:` is an unknown token.

cases.name: filter_fetched_and_unfetched_features
cases.why: Feature rows match only where features were fetched: the lens's and the chassis's Sketch 1 are found; the mast base (one feature, not fetched) is not.

cases.name: filter_features_token
cases.why: `:features`: every fetched feature row.

cases.name: filter_sketches_without_live_part
cases.why: `:sketches` needs a feature `type`: rows from section 7's `features` have none, so nothing matches.

cases.name: filter_root_features
cases.why: A part opened on its own: the root's features match by name.

cases.name: restore_keeps_what_still_exists
cases.why: Kept: rows that can open. Dropped: a row that was deleted, a missing file, a feature key, a folder that does not exist; the order is the visible-row order of the tree with everything open, not the stored order.

cases.name: restore_group_key_with_grouping_off
cases.why: A group key is kept while grouping is off (it only names a row when grouping is on): switching grouping off and on loses nothing.

cases.name: restore_group_that_no_longer_forms
cases.why: A group key whose group no longer has four members is dropped; the first member's own key stays (a part with features opens).

cases.name: restore_row_that_can_no_longer_open
cases.why: A row that cannot open any more (the depth cap stops l1 / l2 / l3, which has no features) is dropped; its ancestors stay.

cases.name: restore_root_is_not_stored
cases.why: The root's key is never an open key.

cases.name: restore_limit
cases.why: At most `limit` keys (2,000 in the app): the first ones in visible-row order are kept, the rest dropped.

cases.name: live_part_alone_collapsed
cases.why: A part opened on its own: Planes always shows (3 default planes + 1 plane feature), Bodies and Curves have items, Surfaces is empty and not listed; folders start collapsed; then the features in build order.

cases.name: live_part_alone_folders_open
cases.why: The folders open: bodies, then the three default planes and the plane feature, then curves; the plane feature also stays in the build order, under its own key.

cases.name: live_part_alone_empty_folders
cases.why: Nothing to put in Bodies, Surfaces or Curves: only Planes is listed.

cases.name: live_part_every_feature_state
cases.why: Every feature state, and several states on one feature: the most severe state wins (lost > moved > pending > rolled back > hidden), `hidden` stays true on the row.

cases.name: live_part_plane_feature_named_xy
cases.why: A plane feature whose id is `xy` (only a hand-written file can have one): the default plane keeps `#plane:xy`; every plane feature in the Planes folder is `#plane:feature:<id>` (here `#plane:feature:xy`), its build-order row `#feature:xy`.

cases.name: live_part_three_levels_down_collapsed
cases.why: The live row is not open: nothing under it is listed, exactly as for any row.

cases.name: live_part_three_levels_down
cases.why: The live part is mast / arm / head, open: its child occurrences first (lens, the missing cable), then its folders, then its features at the same depth; a Part in the same tree stays read-only (the lens's features are section 7's, `type` null).

cases.name: live_part_three_levels_down_folders_open
cases.why: ...with Bodies, Planes and Surfaces open.

cases.name: live_part_leaf_four_deep
cases.why: A live part with no child occurrences, four levels down: the folders and features at depth 5.

cases.name: live_part_at_root_of_assembly
cases.why: The root is live and an assembly: its occurrences, then its Mates and Patterns folders, then the live folders and features.

cases.name: live_part_key_names_no_row
cases.why: The live key names no row of this tree: the inputs are ignored (a `type` null on every row).

cases.name: live_part_on_missing_row
cases.why: A missing row cannot be live and cannot open: nothing is added.

cases.name: live_filter_lost_reference_in_collapsed_live_part
cases.why: `:errors` also matches a lost reference: the collapsed live part is listed open as an ancestor, with the one feature under it (the folders hold no match); the broken mast and missing files match as before.

cases.name: live_filter_warnings_moved_reference
cases.why: `:warnings` also matches a moved reference.

cases.name: live_filter_match_inside_bodies
cases.why: A match inside Bodies lists the folder (open) and the body, and the live part above it.

cases.name: live_filter_default_plane
cases.why: A default plane can match by label; a folder never does.

cases.name: live_filter_plane_feature_twice
cases.why: A plane feature is two rows (build order and the Planes folder): both match, each listed under its parent.

cases.name: live_filter_folder_label_never_matches
cases.why: The word `bodies` is a folder's label: folders never match, so the rows are the root alone.

cases.name: live_filter_sketches
cases.why: `:sketches`: feature rows of type sketch.

cases.name: live_filter_features
cases.why: `:features`: every feature row, the plane feature in both places.

cases.name: live_filter_hidden
cases.why: `:hidden`: hidden features, bodies and default planes (the flag, whatever the state).

cases.name: live_filter_hidden_beneath_a_worse_state
cases.why: A hidden feature whose state is worse still matches `:hidden`, and also `:errors`.

cases.name: live_filter_every_state_errors
cases.why: `:errors` finds lost references only (not moved ones).

cases.name: live_filter_term_and_token
cases.why: A name term and a token on live rows.

cases.name: live_filter_open_keys_ignored
cases.why: The open keys play no part under a filter, for live rows too.

cases.name: live_filter_empty_query
cases.why: An empty query is the live rows for the open keys, every match false.

cases.name: live_restore_folder_key_and_feature_key
cases.why: Folder keys of the live part are open keys (kept when the folder shows); feature, body, plane keys never are; Surfaces has one item, so its key is kept; Curves is empty and not a row, so its key is dropped.

cases.name: live_restore_without_the_live_part
cases.why: The same folder keys without a live part name no rows: dropped.

cases.name: levels_collapsed
cases.why: The default: only the root's folders show (after its children); a collapsed sub-assembly keeps its rolled-up problems bubble.

cases.name: levels_sub_assembly_placed_twice
cases.why: One sub-assembly placed twice, both open: a Mates folder under each placement (two folder keys, boom_l#mates and boom_r#mates), after its children; no Patterns folder (the level has none); each open row's own mates bubble has moved to its folder.

cases.name: levels_folder_open_with_items
cases.why: An open level folder lists its fetched items at depth + 1, keyed <folder>#item:<id>; items carry no bubble and cannot open; held beats near on one item.

cases.name: levels_unfetched_open_folder
cases.why: An open folder whose items are not fetched lists nothing under it (a client may show progress).

cases.name: levels_three_down_every_item_state
cases.why: Three levels down: top's children, then its Mates and Patterns folders, then its fetched features. Every item state: lost (also broken), held (also broken: amber, though the folder's broken count includes it), broken, suppressed, none; a suppressed pattern. A level with patterns and no mates (tower) has only Patterns; open and unfetched, it lists nothing.

cases.name: levels_root_folders_with_items
cases.why: The root's folders, open with items: a Width and a Symmetric mate, a held one; a pattern.

cases.name: levels_grouping_off
cases.why: Grouping makes no difference to the folders.

cases.name: live_part_assembly_with_mates
cases.why: A live assembly row with mates: its children, then its Mates and Patterns folders, then the live part's folders and features; the row's own bubble is on its Mates folder.

cases.name: levels_filter_empty_query
cases.why: An empty query is the rows for the open keys (folders and items as usual), every match false.

cases.name: levels_filter_mates_token
cases.why: `:mates`: every fetched mate item; each folder holding a match is listed open with its ancestors. boom_r's items were not fetched: nothing of it is listed. Patterns never match `:mates`.

cases.name: levels_filter_mates_unfetched
cases.why: `:mates` with nothing fetched: only fetched items can match, so the root alone.

cases.name: levels_filter_errors_three_down
cases.why: `:errors` inside a collapsed branch: the broken hook and pulley, and the lost and broken mates three levels down (the folder and every ancestor listed, open); the held mate that is also broken is amber, not listed.

cases.name: levels_filter_row_without_its_folder
cases.why: A filter lists the open top row (its child matches) but not its Mates folder (no item matches): the row keeps its level's bubble, so a broken mate never vanishes.

cases.name: levels_filter_warnings
cases.why: `:warnings`: near and held items (and the near pin rows); a held mate whose listing says broken is amber.

cases.name: levels_filter_held_and_broken
cases.why: One item both held and broken (top's Distance 1): its state is held, so `:warnings distance` finds it and `:errors` (levels_filter_errors_three_down) does not.

cases.name: levels_filter_suppressed
cases.why: `:suppressed`: a suppressed mate and a suppressed pattern.

cases.name: levels_filter_item_label
cases.why: Items match by label: `width` finds the Width mate only; a folder's own label never matches (`mates`).

cases.name: levels_filter_folder_label
cases.why: `mates` and `patterns` are folders' labels: folders never match themselves.

cases.name: levels_filter_term_and_token
cases.why: A name term and a token on items: `coincident :errors`.

cases.name: levels_restore_nested_folders
cases.why: Folder keys of any level are open keys (kept when the folder shows); an item key never is; a folder the level does not have (tower#mates) is dropped.

cases.name: levels_restore_level_lost_its_mates
cases.why: The same keys after top's mates were deleted: tower/mid/top#mates names no row and is dropped; its Patterns folder stays.

cases.name: mate_names
cases.why: Type N, counted per type in listing order; a mid-plane reference makes a Width mate, counted apart; exactly two references with only the first a mid-plane is Symmetric; an unknown type is written as it is.

cases.name: pattern_names
cases.why: Linear N, Circular N, counted per type in listing order; an unknown type as it is.
